caption:
He lost his sight in Class 8, reading a paragraph aloud. His father left soon after. He never learned Braille - he cracked UPSC anyway.

Manu Garg functioned normally in school until Class 8, when a teacher asked him to read aloud and he realized he could no longer make out the words - he was diagnosed with retinitis pigmentosa, a genetic disorder that progressively destroyed his retinas. Around the same time, his father left the family and many friendships fell away, but his mother remained his unwavering support through mainstream schooling, without either of them ever learning Braille. He relied instead on screen readers and audiobooks through a BA at Hindu College, Delhi University and a postgraduate degree at JNU, where he became a Junior Research Fellow. He failed to clear the UPSC mains on his first attempt in 2023, studied the lesson from that failure and returned in 2024 to secure All India Rank 91 in the Civil Services Examination - entirely through tech-assisted study, with his mother as his central support throughout.
